assumptions: BAGEL2's model: guide counts come from one screen with the stated controls.
The essential and non-essential training sets are appropriate for the cell type.
limits: A Bayes factor ranks genes; the precision and recall curve is what sets a cutoff, and the cutoff is yours.
Low-representation guides weaken a gene's call rather than being dropped silently.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which genes are hits in a pooled CRISPR screen, by gene-level Bayes factor?

description: Call HITS from a pooled CRISPR screen: per-guide read counts in, a gene-level Bayes factor and a precision/recall curve out. This is the other end of a screen from the pool designer — it reads what came back rather than deciding what to order. The estimator is BAGEL2 (Kim & Hart 2021), reproduced byte-for-byte against upstream, so a gene's Bayes factor here is the number BAGEL2 prints for the same counts. It is a COMPARISON against two reference gene sets, not an absolute fitness measure, and it reports how many of those reference genes the library actually carries, because a screen whose gene symbols do not match the reference sets trains on almost nothing and still returns a ranking. MAGeCK's alpha-RRA and drugZ are different statistics that disagree with this one on the same counts; neither is computed here, and a hit list must say which statistic produced it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

control_columns.description: the T0 / plasmid column NAMES, exactly as the header spells them. Summed before the fold change, so a two-replicate T0 is one control and not two.

equalise_replicates.description: scale every Bayes factor as if the screen had this many replicates (upstream's -p), 0 to leave it off. A BF is a SUM over replicates, so two screens of different replicate counts are not comparable until this is set. Advanced.

essential_genes.description: reference ESSENTIAL gene symbols, one per line (extra columns ignored). BAGEL2's CEGv2 is the usual choice; the editor panel ships it and the mouse set beside it.

fdr_cut.description: the false-discovery rate the hit list is cut at. A DISPLAY threshold read off the computed curve, not a parameter of the estimator.

min_reads.description: drop a reagent whose SUMMED control count is below this (upstream's -m). Applied after the pseudocount, exactly as upstream applies it.

non_essential_genes.description: reference NON-ESSENTIAL gene symbols, one per line. BAGEL2's NEGv1 is the usual choice.

pseudo_count.description: added to every count before normalising to 10,000,000 reads per column. Advanced.

read_counts.description: the count table: a header line, then one row per reagent — identifier, gene, then one column per sequenced sample. Tab- or comma-separated. Counts may be written as decimals, as upstream's own files are.

sample_columns.description: which sample column names to score. Leave empty to score every column that is not a control.

name: crispr_analyze_screen

curve.description: the precision/recall curve, one row per gene

fit.description: the fitted line the Bayes factor is scored against: slope, intercept and the fold-change window

genes.description: every gene with its Bayes factor, standard deviation and observation count, ranked

hitBf.description: the Bayes factor the cut lands on (0 when nothing clears the FDR)

hits.description: genes at or above the Bayes factor the FDR cut lands on

training.description: reference essential and non-essential genes FOUND in this library, against the number supplied — the check that the symbols match
